title: "About R²D Science"

---


R<sup>2</sup>D Science is a research and development program built around
**Recursively Realized Distinguishability (R<sup>2</sup>D)**: a mathematical
framework for representing scientific objects in a form that artificial
intelligence can interrogate across disciplines and scales.

Science has powerful mathematics for describing what objects do. What it
largely lacks is a common mathematics for defining what the scientific
object itself is when the boundary of observation changes.

R<sup>2</sup>D addresses that problem by treating microstate, macrostate,
constraint, multiplicity, and recurrence as boundary-dependent mathematical
objects. Changing the boundary therefore does not simply blur or coarse-grain
the same object. It changes the state domain and replaces the scientific
object being described.

## A Mathematical Interface for Science

Artificial intelligence is exceptionally capable at operating on mathematics.
The challenge is that science is presented to AI through many different
physical ontologies: molecules, particles, fields, forces, organisms,
geometries, and other domain-specific objects.

R<sup>2</sup>D provides a common mathematical interface between those
scientific descriptions and AI.

Its purpose is not to replace established scientific laws. It is to transform
the objects appearing in those laws into a common boundary-dependent
mathematical representation so that relationships across disciplines and
scales can be examined directly.

In this sense, R<sup>2</sup>D functions as a front end for AI-driven
scientific discovery.

## From Muscle to a General Framework

R<sup>2</sup>D emerged from research on muscle and molecular motors, where
chemistry, thermodynamics, statistical mechanics, and mechanics can all be
applied to the same biological system while the scientific object changes
with scale.

A myosin molecule can be the object. A collection of molecular motors can be
the object. A muscle fiber can be the object.

The laws remain valid within the boundary where their states and observables
are defined, but the mathematical object itself changes as the boundary
changes.

Formalizing that observation led to a recursive mathematical architecture
that can now be tested far beyond muscle.

## The R<sup>2</sup>D Program

R<sup>2</sup>D Science has four closely connected goals:

1. **Develop the formal framework.**  
   Maintain and extend the R<sup>2</sup>D Canon as the authoritative
   mathematical statement of the theory.

2. **Apply it across science.**  
   Test the same primitive architecture against problems in thermodynamics,
   statistical physics, quantum mechanics, gravity, geometry, fluid mechanics,
   biology, and other domains.

3. **Make the framework usable by AI.**  
   Provide machine-readable versions of the Canon and tools that allow AI to
   retrieve, transform, compare, and interrogate scientific structure using
   R<sup>2</sup>D.

4. **Preserve the development of the theory.**  
   Archive formal releases on Zenodo so that each major stage of the framework
   remains permanently available and citable.

## Read It. Run It. Test It.

R<sup>2</sup>D is intended to be used rather than merely accepted.

**Read R<sup>2</sup>D** to understand the mathematical architecture.

**Run R<sup>2</sup>D** by giving the framework to AI and applying it to a
scientific law, paradox, paper, or unsolved problem.

**Test R<sup>2</sup>D** by asking whether it can preserve established
scientific relationships while removing unnecessary inherited assumptions
about the objects those relationships describe.

**Don't believe R<sup>2</sup>D. Try it.**
